assumptions.obligation: At the start of the trace, i_rst_n is held at 0 for at least 2 i_clk cycles. After that, reset is free and can be asserted again at any time for any length.

notes:
The environment needs only one constraint: ENV-01 holds reset low for the first 2 clock cycles. Nothing else the specification asks of the environment needs an assumption. In detail:
(1) The specification says i_tx_valid does not have to stay high until the handshake, and i_tx_data only matters at the edge where the byte is accepted (UL-7.2-02, UL-7.2-07, UL-12.4-07). So there is no assumption that the byte stays stable while waiting. UL-8.1-04 ('the upstream block waits') describes how the transmitter behaves; it is not a stability rule on the upstream block.
(2) i_rx_ready and i_rxd stay fully free. Overrun, frame errors, glitches, breaks and a low line at reset release are all behaviour the block must handle and report.
(3) UL-12.1-01, 03, 04 and 05 (synchronous reset release, no X/Z values, i_rxd moved away from clock edges) need no assumption here. The formal model is synchronous and only uses 0 and 1, so these always hold.
(4) There is no assumption for the PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT range (UL-10.8-02, UL-4-01). It is a fixed parameter, not an input. Assuming a false constant would make every proof pass vacuously. The range check belongs to the block's elaboration error (UL-4-04) and to the configuration you choose: 4..65535.
(5) The env_init_cnt helper is not cleared by the DUT reset. This is on purpose: if it re-armed on every reset, every later reset would be forced to last 2 cycles. That would hide behaviour after mid-frame resets lasting a single cycle (UL-12.3-04).
